blindComparison: A stranger picks the reference frame, immediately, and the single specific reason is that nothing in our frame is attached to the ground. In Tsushima's golden-hour shrine approach the low sun rakes across the flagstone and every post, lantern and tree throws a long shadow that is dark but blue — filled by the sky — so the objects sit IN the world. Ours: I scanned the flagstone across the base of the two foreground stone lanterns in `phone-torii-r7.png` at y=0.955 in 0.025-wide steps and got p50 luma 12.4 / 44.3 / 30.3 / 24.1 / 9.7 / 21.4 / 54.6 / 28.2 — the lantern's own footprint (44.3) is a LOCAL MAXIMUM. The ground directly under a 2.5 m stone lantern is 4.5x brighter than open ground 210 px away. There is no contact darkening, no cast shadow, no cavity. And where shadows DO land (the banner-pole shadow in `phone-sun-r7.png`) they measure RGB 37.8,21.9,11.8 against lit sand at 113.6,72.5,38.1 — a shadow that is 7.4% of key brightness and, at R/B 3.20 vs the lit surface's 2.98, is actually WARMER than the light it is hiding from. That is not a shadow, that is the albedo multiplied toward black. ARCHITECTURE §5 binds shadow/ambient to #4a6b8f (R/B 0.52). The result is that all five frames read as brown mud with props floating on it, while the reference reads as gold light and blue shade. Everything else on this list is downstream of that.

findings.shot: all five (worst in phone-torii-r7, phone-sun-r7, phone-hero-r7)
findings.problem: The clouds are not clouds. They are dozens of small, isolated, hard-edged elliptical lozenges, each roughly 120x40 px, each with a sharp leading edge and a directionally-smeared tail, scattered on a flat sky gradient at a near-regular pitch. They never merge into a cloud mass, they have no soft feathering, no internal structure, no vertical build, and no variation in size or shape. Crop shots/phone-torii-r7.png at 0.62,0.02,0.36,0.26 to see it at native: the blobs there are dark grey-mauve with muddy red-brown cores and read as coffee stains or blood smears on a lens. Crop shots/phone-sun-r7.png at 0.02,0.10,0.42,0.28 and it is the same shapes in cream-brown. Worse, they are consistently DARKER than the sky they sit on, including in the sun-facing half of phone-sun-r7 where clouds within 30 degrees of a low sun must be the brightest objects in the sky. The sky behind them is essentially achromatic: shots/phone-sun-r7.png 0.02,0.10,0.42,0.28 measures mean RGB 174.5,180.8,177.9 with saturation 0.049; region 0.05,0.30,0.12,0.20 measures 159.6,160.5,154.8 saturation 0.069. That is neutral grey paint, in a frame that is looking into a magic-hour sun. The sky occupies 30-50% of hero, torii and sun. This is the first thing a viewer's eye lands on and it reads as a bug.
findings.why: Every reference frame this build is judged against sells its hour through the sky: Tsushima's stratus banks lit warm on their undersides against a graded cyan-to-amber field, Sekiro's Ashina dusk with layered cloud depth. A field of identical dark lozenges on a grey field is the single loudest 'this is a tech demo' signal in the set, and no amount of ground detail recovers from it.
findings.fix: Two separate targets. (1) Cloud FORM: the cloud layer must produce connected, multi-scale masses with soft edges — at native resolution I must not be able to trace an individual blob's outline. Target: no closed cloud shape smaller than ~15% of frame width, edges feathered over at least 40 px, and at least three octaves of internal density variation so a single cloud has bright and dark regions within itself. (2) Cloud SHADING: at the current sun elevation the cloud bases and sun-facing flanks must be BRIGHTER and warmer than the clear sky next to them, not darker. Concrete check: sample the sky in phone-sun-r7's framing at 0.30,0.30,0.15,0.20 (currently mean 199.9,193.4,183.5, R-B = 16) — after the fix, cloud pixels in the sun-facing half must reach R-B >= 50 and exceed the adjacent clear-sky luma, and clear sky within ~30 degrees of the sun must reach saturation >= 0.25 (currently 0.049-0.069). Away from the sun the sky should still go cool, so the frame carries a warm-to-cool gradient rather than one grey value.

findings.shot: all five (measured in phone-sun-r7, phone-torii-r7, phone-hero-r7)
findings.problem: Shadowed surfaces receive no cool fill anywhere in the set. They are the lit albedo multiplied down toward black, keeping the same orange hue. Measurements, all same-surface before/after pairs inside one frame: (a) phone-sun-r7, the long banner-pole shadow on the sand — inside shadow 0.365,0.900,0.035,0.02 = RGB 37.8,21.9,11.8, luma p50 7.2; lit sand 40 px away 0.365,0.865,0.035,0.02 = RGB 113.6,72.5,38.1, luma p50 96.9. Shadow is 7.4% of key. R/B ratio: shadow 3.20, lit 2.98 — the shadow is warmer than the key. (b) phone-hero-r7, ground under the left pavilion 0.02,0.63,0.10,0.06 = RGB 24.6,19.8,18.4 vs open ground at the same depth 0.30,0.63,0.10,0.06 = RGB 57.6,45.3,38.4. (c) phone-torii-r7 flagstone scan at y=0.955: the darkest patches are RGB 21.4,12.9,7.5 and 37.6,20.4,6.5 — pure orange-black. ARCHITECTURE §5 binds shadow/ambient to #4a6b8f, which is R/B 0.52. Measured R/B in shadow across the set is 1.3 to 3.2. Nowhere in 2532x1170 x 5 frames did I find a cool shadow. The consequence is visible without any probe: the frames have exactly one colour temperature, so there is no read of 'sun' versus 'shade', and the whole set collapses into brown mud. phone-valley-r7 is the extreme case — it is a single orange hue edge to edge with 0.000% of pixels above luma 240, i.e. not one clean highlight in 2.96 million pixels.
findings.why: Warm key against cool sky-bounce fill is the entire colour engine of both reference titles — it is what makes Tsushima's grass read gold and its shade read blue in the same frame. Without it, a magic-hour scene reads as a monochrome sepia photograph, and no amount of texture detail can put the hour back.
findings.fix: Shadowed and sky-facing surfaces must be lit by a distinctly blue ambient/fill, and it must be strong enough to survive the grade. Verifiable target, measured on the same two regions I used above in phone-sun-r7: (1) shadowed sand at 0.365,0.900,0.035,0.02 must come up from luma p50 7.2 to p50 25-40 — a key:fill ratio of roughly 4:1, not 13.5:1; (2) its R/B ratio must invert from 3.20 to below 1.0, i.e. B must exceed R in shadow. Same test on phone-hero-r7 0.02,0.63,0.10,0.06 (currently 24.6,19.8,18.4) — after the fix B must be the largest channel there. Re-measure both regions before and after; if the numbers come back byte-identical the branch you edited is not lighting those pixels.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED, disprove before acting: the fill may be a single hemisphere/ambient term whose colour is being multiplied by the same warm sun colour as the key, or the tonemap/grade may be applying a warm curve after the fill so any blue that is present gets pulled back to orange. Check whether blue survives at the point the fill is added, before the grade, and separately after the grade — that isolates which of the two is eating it.

findings.problem: The bamboo sea — the headline element of ARCHITECTURE §5's setting — fails on three independent counts, all confirmed at native. (1) CULMS TERMINATE IN MID-AIR. Crop shots/phone-valley-r7.png at 0.30,0.20,0.16,0.22 (405x257 native). The culms at crop-x 75, 95, 110, 340 and 355 run down from the canopy and stop dead at crop-y 205, 200, 185, 150, 145 respectively, on a clean flat horizontal cut, with unbroken lit sand clearly visible below and behind them. There is no ridge line or occluder — they are hovering above the terrain. The same defect is visible in the wider crop 0.10,0.28,0.45,0.30 at crop-x 440, 590, 625, 900, 930, 960 and 1030. Floating geometry is the single most amateur-reading defect a frame can carry. (2) DETACHED LEAF CARDS LITTERING THE SKY. Crop shots/phone-valley-r7.png at 0.28,0.03,0.34,0.30 — there are at least twelve small dark leaf sprites suspended in open sky with no culm attached, at crop coords approximately (110,10) (250,105) (300,120) (390,55) (430,80) (470,110) (520,95) (600,120) (640,105) (800,175) (835,190). Same thing in shots/phone-wide-r7.png crop 0.00,0.20,0.30,0.25 at roughly (135,10) (200,15) (255,35) (300,30) (390,40) (420,45) (555,55) (600,65) (665,80) (710,95) (735,100), and again in phone-sun-r7 crop 0.55,0.45,0.30,0.16. Against pale sky they read as dead pixels or dirt on the sensor. (3) NO DENSITY. In the wide crop 0.00,0.20,0.30,0.25 more than half the hillside surface is bare pink-brown dirt showing between squat, near-identical, same-height green clumps on a visibly regular scatter. In the valley crop you can see straight through the grove to open sand. A bamboo sea must be an opaque wall of culms.
findings.why: Tsushima's bamboo strike is a solid green wall of tall, near-vertical, size-varied culms that completely occludes the ground and reads as one mass at thumbnail size. Ours reads as a scrubby hillside with weeds on it, and it is additionally broken in a way a player will notice in the first five seconds: plants hanging in the air and specks of dirt floating in the sky.
findings.fix: Three checkable targets. (1) Every culm's base must be at or below the terrain surface at its own XZ — re-crop shots/phone-valley-r7.png at 0.30,0.20,0.16,0.22 after the fix and there must be zero culms that end above visible ground. Sink bases ~0.3 m into the terrain so there is no seam. (2) Zero leaf cards may render without their culm: after the fix, crop 0.28,0.03,0.34,0.30 of the valley framing and the open sky above the canopy must contain no isolated dark sprites. (3) Density: in the phone-wide-r7 framing, region 0.00,0.20,0.30,0.25 currently shows bare dirt through more than half its area — raise culm count/clumping and add height variation (a 2:1 tall-to-short spread) until bare ground is not visible through the grove at that framing. Also give the culms real vertical bias: several are currently leaning 20-40 degrees off vertical, which reads as broken rather than windblown — cap the lean at roughly 8 degrees and drive the rest of the motion from bend, not tilt.

findings.problem: Large areas of ground are a single flat wash with no macro content at all. (a) phone-valley-r7: crop 0.10,0.28,0.45,0.30 — that is 13.5% of the frame and it contains one uniform orange-brown surface carrying a single high-frequency stipple that visibly repeats at a regular pitch, like sandpaper. No rocks, no roots, no fallen leaves, no puddles, no path, no moss, no colour variation, nothing. The whole lower half of that frame is the same. Numerically it is not lack of noise but lack of RANGE: the mid-ground slope 0.30,0.33,0.28,0.13 measures luma p1 73.6 -> p99 148.4, a 75-value band, while the foreground flagstone in the SAME frame at 0.30,0.86,0.28,0.13 spans p1 9.8 -> p99 110.9, a 101-value band with real darks. The slope has neither black nor white in it. (b) phone-wide-r7: crop 0.50,0.55,0.30,0.28 — the right two-thirds of that crop is a featureless dark olive-grey field with literally nothing on it, measuring mean RGB 46.9,40.2,33.3, saturation 0.282, detail 4.68, against the foreground path in the same frame at 0.30,0.80,0.20,0.16 which measures 68,43.1,29.8, saturation 0.525, detail 7.43. That field is roughly 20% of the frame. It is presumably meant to be the moss/grass of §5's palette (#4e6b3c, a clear green) but measures brown-grey with a green channel below the red.
findings.why: Both reference titles carry ground detail at every scale — Tsushima's fields have wind-combed grass, scattered rock, colour breakup and mud tracks; Sekiro's courtyards have moss in the joints and worn paths. A 1.8 km vista whose floor is one flat brown value is the thing that most immediately says 'level editor', and it removes the mid-tone interest that the composition needs to lead the eye.
findings.fix: The ground needs macro variation, not more grain. Concretely: (1) break the splat with at least two additional surface types at 10-40 m scale — exposed rock, darker damp soil, leaf/needle litter under the grove — so the valley slope in crop 0.10,0.28,0.45,0.30 stops being one hue. Target: raise that region's lumaSpread from 74.9 toward the 101 the foreground flagstone already achieves in the same frame, with real values below luma 40 present. (2) Kill the visible tiling: at native the stipple repeats at a fixed pitch — break it with a second, much lower-frequency modulation so no motif is recognisable twice in one crop. (3) The plateau field in phone-wide-r7 region 0.50,0.55,0.30,0.28 must actually read as moss/grass ground: green channel above red, saturation up from 0.282 toward 0.45, and some scattered surface breakup so it is not a single value. Re-measure both regions before and after.

findings.problem: Every lit lantern in the set is a hard-edged, clipped, neutral-white blob with essentially no bloom. Measured: the hanging paper lantern in phone-torii-r7 at 0.535,0.53,0.035,0.06 is RGB 231.8,224.4,210.3, luma p50 252.8 and p99 254.6, saturation 0.111 — that is white, clipped, with an 8% warm tint that is invisible. The torii lantern in phone-hero-r7 at 0.735,0.505,0.03,0.05 is the same story (201,195.8,180.8, p50 231.6). Crop shots/phone-sun-r7.png at 0.55,0.45,0.30,0.16 and look at the lantern edge against the sky: it is one pixel from 255 to sky, with no glow skirt at all. I profiled the falloff to the right of the big lantern in phone-sun-r7 at y=0.40: x=0.712 p50 176.5, x=0.724 169.7, x=0.736 167.3, x=0.760 161.6 — a 15/255 drop over 228 px, which is indistinguishable from the sky's own gradient. There is also no light leaving these sources: in crop 0.00,0.62,0.35,0.38 of phone-torii-r7 the stone eaves DIRECTLY ABOVE each lit paper panel are dark, and the ground under each lantern is not warmed at all. ARCHITECTURE §5 item 7 requires 'bloom with a soft, wide, non-blown falloff' and these are the exact opposite: blown and narrow.
findings.why: Warm paper lanterns against a cooling dusk sky are the signature image of both reference titles' shrine approaches, and they work because the light BLEEDS — a wide amber halo that softens the lantern's own silhouette and pools on the stone below. A clipped white ovoid with a hard edge reads as an unlit plastic egg with an emissive material on it, and it is the brightest object in three of five frames, so it dominates the read.
findings.fix: The bloom pass must produce a wide, soft, warm skirt off these sources — the source already clips at 252-254 so there is plenty above any sane threshold. Verifiable target on phone-sun-r7's framing: profiling right from the big lantern at y=0.40, the luma at x=0.712 should sit at least 50 above the far-sky baseline at x=0.800, and the falloff should still be measurable 250-350 px out rather than dying in 15 values. The skirt must be warm — sample the halo 30 px off the lantern edge and R-B should be >= 40, so the glow carries §5's #ffd9a8 key colour rather than the source's neutral white. Keep the falloff smooth: no visible ring or step in the halo, and no square kernel artefacts at the frame edge.

findings.problem: The sakura canopy — the largest single object in phone-hero-r7, occupying roughly 12% of the frame — is a flat-lit mauve blob. Crop shots/phone-hero-r7.png at 0.04,0.02,0.30,0.42 and at native you can count the individual quads: hard straight polygon edges are plainly visible across the mass, and the blossom texture is one repeating ~12 px pink circle motif tiled on every card, so it reads as bubble wrap rather than blossom. It has no form: the sunward top at 0.09,0.06,0.10,0.06 measures luma p50 131.9 and the shaded underside at 0.14,0.32,0.10,0.06 measures p50 108.7 — a ratio of 0.82, i.e. an 18% value break between the top and the bottom of a tree at magic hour. There is also no branch structure reading through, no light-through-leaf translucency, and black alpha speckles inside the canopy at approximately (485,375) (600,340) (630,325) (655,300) in that crop. Colour is wrong too: the canopy core at 0.10,0.10,0.16,0.20 is RGB 137.1,94.4,107.8 — blue exceeds green by 14, so the mass reads dull violet-grey, not warm cream-pink. In phone-wide-r7 (crop 0.30,0.36,0.22,0.20) the same tree is a solid opaque cauliflower of pink with no gaps at all; squint at it and it reads as a cumulus cloud stuck on the shrine roof, failing the thumbnail silhouette test.
findings.why: The sakura is the emotional centre of this composition and the one object the eye goes to first. In Tsushima a blossom canopy has a blown warm crown, a deep cool underside, dark branch structure cutting through it and visible sky holes — it has volume. Ours has none of those, so the most important object in the hero frame is also the least believable one in it.
findings.fix: Give the canopy form and the right hue. (1) Value break: after the fix, the sunward top (phone-hero-r7 region 0.09,0.06,0.10,0.06) versus the underside (0.14,0.32,0.10,0.06) must be at least a 3:1 luma ratio, i.e. underside p50 no higher than ~45 when the top is ~132 — self-shadowing or a baked per-card ambient-occlusion gradient down the canopy, whichever you own. (2) Hue: the canopy core at 0.10,0.10,0.16,0.20 must move from B>G to R>G>B with R-B >= 40, so it reads warm cream-pink at this hour rather than mauve. (3) Break the mass: sky must be visible through the canopy in gaps, and dark branch geometry must read through it — the wide-framing silhouette (crop 0.30,0.36,0.22,0.20) must stop being a closed convex blob. (4) Fix the black speckles inside the canopy and the crunchy 1-pixel alpha cutoff on the card silhouettes.

findings.problem: This is the shot framed directly into a low sun, with a torii post, a shimenawa rope, two banner flags and a bamboo line all between camera and sun, and it produces no volumetric light at all. Crop shots/phone-sun-r7.png at 0.24,0.28,0.26,0.55 and look: there is exactly one thin diagonal anamorphic streak running from about crop (555,155) to (490,330), and nothing else. No shafts fanning from the sun, no light scattering through the rope or between the banners, no dust in the beam. There is also no sun disc anywhere in the frame — the sun sits behind the torii post and the post's edge against the bright sky at crop x~500-520, y 100-350 is a hard, clean, dark line with zero bloom bleed or light-wrap around it, which is exactly what a low sun immediately behind a thin occluder cannot look like. Supporting numbers: the sky 10 degrees off the sun position (region 0.30,0.30,0.15,0.20) measures mean RGB 199.9,193.4,183.5 — R minus B of 16, essentially white — with p99 luma only 224, so there is no bright, warm, scattering core anywhere near the sun. ARCHITECTURE §5 lists 'volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo' as non-negotiable item 4 and 'a real sun disc' as part of item 1; on this framing, which exists specifically to show them, both are absent.
findings.why: The into-the-sun torii silhouette with shafts breaking around the posts is THE marketing frame of this genre — it is on the box of both reference titles. Delivering that framing with a hard-edged black post on a flat pale sky and one thin lens line is the largest single gap between this set and the bar, because the composition promises the effect and then does not pay it off.
findings.fix: Produce real radial scattering from the sun position in this framing. Verifiable targets on shots/phone-sun-r7.png's exact camera: (1) visible shafts must fan from behind the torii post across the sky region 0.24,0.28,0.26,0.55, with the gaps between the two banner flags and under the shimenawa reading as distinct bright wedges — after the fix I must be able to see the occluders' shapes written into the light. (2) The sky immediately around the sun (region 0.30,0.30,0.15,0.20, currently mean 199.9,193.4,183.5 / R-B 16 / p99 224) must gain a hot warm core: R-B >= 60 and p99 luma at 250+. (3) The occluding post edge must show light wrap — sample a 10 px strip on the post just inside its silhouette at the sun's height and it must be measurably lifted relative to the same post 300 px lower. Do not raise the effect by adding a constant emission floor; the shafts must be zero where the sky is fully occluded.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED, disprove before acting: the sun may be sitting fully behind the torii post in the occluder buffer, so a screen-space radial pass has no source pixel to smear and correctly outputs nothing. Before changing weights, check whether the sun's screen position in this pose is inside an occluded texel — if it is, the fix is to let scattering originate from the sun's screen position even when occluded, not to raise gain. Raising the pass weight without checking this made the frame worse on a previous occasion.

findings.problem: In the torii pose, foreground and mid-ground props sit on the ground with no shadow and no contact occlusion of any kind. Crop shots/phone-torii-r7.png at 0.00,0.62,0.35,0.38: the two large stone lanterns meet the flagstone with no darkening at all — I scanned the ground along y=0.955 in 0.025-wide steps from x=0.035 to x=0.228 and got p50 luma 12.4 / 44.3 / 30.3 / 24.1 / 9.7 / 21.4 / 54.6 / 28.2. The left lantern's footprint sits at x=0.062-0.090 and is a LOCAL MAXIMUM (44.3), 4.5x brighter than the open flagstone at x=0.145 (9.7). The variation in that scan tracks the flagstone texture, not the objects standing on it. The same is true across the whole courtyard in crop 0.25,0.72,0.45,0.28: neither torii post throws a shadow, and the shrine building in the background throws nothing onto the ground in front of it. In phone-valley-r7 (crop 0.30,0.20,0.16,0.22) not one bamboo culm darkens the sand it stands on — the sand under the grove measures the same as the open sand beside it. Shadows clearly exist elsewhere in the build (the banner pole in phone-sun-r7 and the balustrade in phone-valley-r7 both cast), so this is selective, not global. ARCHITECTURE §5 items 2 and 3 require contact-hardening on the near cascade and ground-truth-ish AO in crevices; in this pose neither is reaching the frame.
findings.why: This is the exact failure CRITIC.md names as the archetype: with no tight contact darkening where an object meets the ground, everything looks pasted on rather than standing on the surface. Four two-and-a-half-metre stone lanterns hovering shadowless in the foreground of the shot most likely to be used as a key art frame is disqualifying on its own.
findings.fix: Every prop that meets the ground in this pose must produce a dark, tight contact at its base plus a directional cast shadow. Verifiable target: re-run the scan on shots/phone-torii-r7.png along y=0.955 in 0.025 steps from x=0.035 to x=0.228 — after the fix, the two lantern footprints must be LOCAL MINIMA, at most 40% of the open-flagstone p50 either side of them, instead of the current local maxima. Separately, both torii posts and the four foreground stone lanterns must throw visible directional cast shadows across the flagstone in crop 0.25,0.72,0.45,0.28, consistent in direction with the key light that is warming the torii's upper beam. Verify by measuring the same regions before and after; identical numbers mean the pass you edited is not touching these pixels.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED, disprove before acting: because shadows DO appear in phone-sun-r7 and phone-valley-r7 but not in this pose, the near cascade may not be covering the foreground at this camera height/pitch, or the props in this pose may not be in the shadow-caster set. Check which cascade the lantern bases fall into for this exact camera before assuming the shadow term itself is wrong.
